annotations.text:
PAPER & INK

Depth from SHAPE — a 2px outline and a hard offset shadow, so every card is a physical piece on a table. Fredoka + Nunito.

Inverts cleanly, because geometry does not care which way round the ground is. Reads younger and more playful.

DEEP TABLE

Depth from LIGHT — glow, glass, one gold accent per screen. Gabarito + Manrope.

Dark is its native mode. In light the glow has to become a cast shadow instead, which is a translation rather than an inversion — look at how much quieter the light version is than the dark one. That gap is the honest cost of this direction.

CONTRAST, MEASURED

All four builds clear WCAG AA at 4.5:1.

Deep Table's light build failed first time — its faint text came out at 2.80:1, because 42% white on a dark ground is fine and 45% dark on white is not. The alphas were solved for, not nudged by eye. That is the trap in every light/dark pair.

Paper & Ink carried through two more screens, both modes.

The battle screen is not drawn: its chrome is two score pills and a hint line, and the screen is almost entirely the 3D board, which does not change with the theme.
